*.note: P1: v0.3.6 through v0.3.16 arrow integer widths disagree with today's, and below v0.3.6 no arrow writer exists; P2: v0.3.16's parquet writer adds the `data` column unconditionally, fixed in v0.3.17, and below that the no-CDC drivers' parquet output lacks _cdc_timestamp

rules.note: olake's write and sync stamps: wall-clock, never value-comparable across two runs
kafka's broker receive time, and offsets whose assignment order varies across concurrent partition writes
s3's cursor IS the object's upload stamp; each run uploads its own copy
iceberg column types: #1233, the legacy writer truncated timestamps to milliseconds; the candidate keeps microseconds

oracle.note: P2 for a no-CDC driver: below v0.3.17 the parquet output lacks _cdc_timestamp, and v0.3.11's writer panics feeding an int64 into an INT32 column on the incremental path

rules.note: id is the seed's identity column: its implicit sequence caches 20 values, so a cache discard between two inserts resumes at the high water mark and the two sides disagree; _olake_id uses that single primary key verbatim, so it is as non-deterministic as id

mysql.note: M2 (ENUM serialization, fixed v0.3.9) and M3 (DECIMAL/NUMERIC via float32, fixed v0.3.7) need no rule: both thresholds sit below v0.3.11, the oldest release with a state version update

rules.note: non-UTF-8 charset bytes reach the writer as invalid UTF-8; gRPC marshal fails, retry backoff looks like a hang
the binlog path decoded latin1 as ISO-8859-1 instead of MySQL's cp1252 until #1280, so bytes 0x80-0x9F arrived as C1 controls; below v0.7.2 latin1 also failed as invalid UTF-8, like ucs2/utf16le
M1: SET columns emitted the numeric bitmask on the binlog path before the fix
unsigned MEDIUMINT was sign-extended on the binlog path before v0.9.3 (-1 where the value is 16777215)
binary columns were carried as text before binary support (#1183): non-UTF-8 bytes fail the legacy writer's gRPC marshal and the retry backoff looks like a hang

BIGINT UNSIGNED at or above 2^63 reaches the incremental scan as a byte slice; before v0.9.0 (state v6, ReformatInt64) it cannot be converted: v0.3.11's Iceberg writer fatals on the mixed long/string batch and a candidate on an older state file retries into a hang

mongodb.note: G1 (BSON regex serialized with Go field names, not lowercase keys, fixed v0.3.14) needs no rule: its threshold sits below the v0.3.17 floor

rules.note: _id is a server-generated ObjectID, so it cannot match across two independent runs; _olake_id hashes it, so it is as non-deterministic as its source

kafka.note: v0.3.12 added decoder.UseNumber() but the flattener only learned json.Number in v0.3.16; pre-v0.3.12 numbers all typed double against today's catalog

db2.note: first release carrying the driver; refine after the first sweep if early db2 images are missing from the registry

rules.note: older discovers type DECFLOAT number while the candidate reads it as String, so the upgraded incremental sync fatals on the mixed batch

s3.note: v0.9.2 is the first release carrying the driver and the XML source format landed in v0.9.3; the v0.9.1 parquet fixes need no rule, as they sit below this floor: a group-typed column (map_col, struct_col, list_col) panicked the parser on Kind(), and INT96 (int96_col) was discovered as timestamptz while the reader handed back a string, which the iceberg flush rejects
